purpose: How a commercial cleaning broker decides which facilities to pursue and when to walk away, converts a physical walkthrough into a measured scope and a defensible labor-load and cost build, and turns that build into a priced proposal and a set of contract terms that keep a monthly spread intact for the life of the agreement without ever misrepresenting who actually performs the cleaning.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the revenue unit is one recurring monthly commercial cleaning contract sold to a facility and delivered by contracted crews the broker arranges; the broker keeps the spread between the client's monthly price and the delivered cost, so every acquisition decision is judged by whether that spread survives the whole term rather than by whether the bid was won

no price, wage, production rate, per-square-foot number, spread percentage, market size or account multiple in this knowledge base is a market rate or an industry benchmark; each is a MECHANISM the broker measures inside its own quotes, walkthroughs and delivered costs and re-measures for every contract

worker classification, insurance, bonding, licensing and facility-specific compliance duties are named only as obligation CLASSES; each varies by jurisdiction, facility type, landlord and year, must be verified with a qualified professional and the current authority before anything is promised, and is never carried over from a prior deal by assumption

the buyer is told before signing that cleaning is performed by contracted crews the broker arranges, supervises and stands behind; nothing in this acquisition method depends on the buyer misunderstanding the service model

buyers vary widely in sophistication within the same commercial market - a solo practice owner, a volunteer board treasurer and a regional facilities department read the same contract differently - so the duty to explain scope, exclusions, term and cancellation in plain language scales with that gap

margin is created at bid time and only defended afterwards: a mis-measured, mis-scoped or under-priced bid is a problem the crew and the client both live with for the whole term, which is why scoping rigor sits upstream of everything else here
this knowledge base is educational business-process knowledge; it is not personalized legal, tax, insurance or financial advice for any particular broker, contract or jurisdiction
exclusions: sourcing, vetting, quoting and engaging the crews or subcontractors who perform the work, the engagement-structure decision itself, the crew-facing scope handoff pack, inspection and walkthrough cadence once an account is live, quality scoring, supplies and equipment responsibility models on the delivery side, and backup coverage when a crew fails: owned by the crew sourcing, quality control and walkthroughs knowledge base

month-to-month margin health of a live contract including crew cost drift, scope creep and complaint load as mechanisms, the complaint-response system as a retention engine, renewal and repricing conversations, account expansion into added frequency, add-on services and sister sites, and the decision to exit an unprofitable contract: owned by the margin management, client retention and renewals knowledge base

any statement of what a cleaning contract costs, what a crew is paid, what a production rate is, what a spread should be, or how large a local cleaning market is, presented as a figure of fact rather than as a mechanism the broker measures in its own bids

legal conclusions about worker classification, insurance adequacy, bonding, contract enforceability, indemnity allocation or facility compliance duties for any particular deal, arrangement or jurisdiction; these are flagged for verification by a qualified professional, never resolved here

sales tactics that depend on a buyer's fear, urgency or confusion: health-scare and inspection-failure framing used as a closing lever, invented liability threats, unevidenced disparagement of an incumbent, deliberately vague scope written to make a price look low, and any implication that the broker's own employees clean the building when contracted crews do
performing the cleaning itself: chemical selection, equipment operation, floor-care technique, infection-control procedure and any operational instruction to a cleaner

residential and household cleaning, one-off consumer jobs, and franchise-system purchase decisions, all of which have different buyers, economics and obligation classes than the commercial contracts this knowledge base bids

glossary.definition: The area a crew actually cleans, by surface type, excluding walls, shafts, unfinished storage, areas billed to other tenants and any space the crew never enters; it is the denominator of the labor model and is not the leased or gross figure a client reads off a lease.

The area or fixture volume one worker completes for a given task per hour at the required standard; it is an input carrying a source and an uncertainty, drawn from published references, crew quotes or the broker's own timed observations, never a universal constant.

The adjustment applied to a production rate for what is physically in the way - cubicle density, desk clutter, stacked stock, equipment on floors - because obstruction, more than area, is what makes a borrowed rate wrong for a specific building.

The scope of work written as task by area by frequency, with an explicit exclusion list; it is simultaneously the thing being priced, the instruction the crew receives and the standard against which any complaint is judged.

Cycle-based services outside the nightly or weekly routine - carpet extraction, burnishing, strip and refinish, window cleaning, pressure washing, post-construction cleanup - which consume hours in a lump and must be priced on their own line or amortized deliberately.

A cleaner stationed at a site during business hours for restroom checks, spills, entrance upkeep and trash, priced as staffed hours rather than by production rate, and a common scope element in high-traffic retail, medical and multi-tenant buildings.

Everything the broker actually pays or absorbs to serve one site for one month: the crew line, plus supplies and equipment where the contract assigns them to the broker, travel and inspection trips, backfill, billing effort and the complaint time the account consumes.

The difference between the client's monthly price and the delivered cost; it is not profit until it has funded acquisition effort, administration, inspections, the response commitment, backfill risk, bad debt and broker-level insurance, and it behaves differently as a fixed amount than as a percentage as costs rise.

glossary.term: certificate of insurance and additional-insured status
glossary.definition: The document class by which a client is shown that coverage exists, and the endorsement class by which the client is added to another party's policy; the specific limits, forms and endorsements demanded vary by client, landlord, facility class and jurisdiction and are verified per contract rather than assumed.

The price below which this specific site will not be bid, computed from the cost build and the sensitivity tests and fixed before any price conversation, so that a negotiation compares against a number that already exists instead of producing one under pressure.

nodes.definition: Fix what the business sells and where the money it keeps comes from, before any prospecting begins. The revenue unit is one recurring monthly cleaning contract; what is sold is a managed outcome - a building cleaned to a written standard with a named person accountable when it is not - rather than hours of labor resold; and what is kept is the spread between the client's monthly price and the delivered cost once the crew is paid and every obligation the contract leaves with the broker is absorbed. This unit writes down three things the rest of the subdomain depends on: what a good contract means for this broker (a spread that survives the term, a site that can actually be staffed and inspected, a buyer who pays), the standing conditions under which the broker will not bid at all, and the principle that margin is created at bid time and only ever defended afterwards - a mis-scoped bid is a full-term problem that no amount of later account management repairs. It also fixes the shared vocabulary the whole acquisition process uses: cleanable area, task-and-frequency matrix, labor load, delivered cost, spread and walk-away floor.

included: the recurring contract as the revenue unit
the cost classes the spread must absorb
the margin-is-made-at-bid-time principle
the standing will-not-bid conditions
the shared vocabulary for scoping and pricing
excluded: crew sourcing, vetting and pricing, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
monthly margin monitoring and renewal decisions on live accounts, owned by the retention knowledge base
any spread percentage, price point or margin figure stated as typical for the trade

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the first cycle of bid-versus-delivered-cost comparisons shows the spread absorbing cost classes the charter never named

pros.claim: Naming every cost class the spread must absorb before prospecting stops the classic broker error of pricing against the crew quote alone
pros.example: a bid that covers the crew payment but not the monthly inspection drive, the paper goods the contract assigns to the broker, or the hour a single complaint consumes

cons.claim: A frame written once hardens into a rule of thumb and stops being re-measured as crew quotes, facility mix and obligations change
cons.example: a broker still assuming the cost shape of its first small office contract while bidding a medical suite with waste-handling duties and stricter certificate demands

failure_modes: treating the business as a labor reseller and pricing hours instead of a managed outcome
assuming a thin bid can be repaired at renewal, which exports a bid-time error into the retention system
leaving the will-not-bid conditions unwritten so every marginal lead is chased in a slow month
acceptance_tests: the charter states the revenue unit, every cost class the spread must absorb, and at least three standing conditions under which the broker will not bid, and it carries a date
revisit_triggers: crew quotes or supply costs in a territory move enough to change what the spread must absorb
the broker adds a facility class whose cost classes differ from the ones the charter names

nodes.definition: Tell the buyer, in writing and in the room, how the service is actually delivered: who engages the people who will be alone in their building, who supervises them, who carries which insurance class, who the client calls at ten at night, and who is accountable when a night is missed. This is a unit of work rather than a disclaimer - it produces a disclosure sentence that sits in the proposal itself, a truthful answer given every time the employment question is asked, and a standing prohibition on letting a competitive story imply an in-house workforce the broker does not have. It is also self-protective: a client who understood the model at signing reads a scheduled crew change as ordinary staffing news, while a client who was allowed to believe otherwise reads the same event as a discovered deception and treats the whole relationship as suspect. The unit decides what must be disclosed - the delivery model, the accountability path, the insurance and background-check CLASSES actually verified for this contract - and what remains ordinary commercial confidence, namely crew pricing and the broker's own spread.

included: the written disclosure sentence in the proposal
the truthful answer to the employment question
the named accountability path
the line between disclosure and legitimate commercial confidence
excluded: the engagement-structure decision and its legal analysis, which belong to the crew sourcing knowledge base and a qualified professional
complaint handling once the account is live, owned by the retention knowledge base
promises about specific crew members the arrangement cannot guarantee

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a buyer's reaction after signing shows the disclosure language was not understood the way it was written

pros.claim: A client who knew the model at signing absorbs a crew change as normal operations instead of discovering a hidden fact
pros.example: a property manager told at bid time that a vetted crew partner staffs the site, who then reads a scheduled crew swap as a staffing note rather than a bait-and-switch

cons.claim: Plain disclosure loses some bids to competitors who let the buyer assume an in-house team
cons.example: a buyer who says he only wants a company's own employees in the building and awards the contract elsewhere once told the truth

failure_modes: letting the phrase our team do the work of implying employment
disclosing only when the question is asked directly rather than in the document
describing the model correctly in conversation while sending a proposal that reads as in-house
acceptance_tests: every proposal contains a written sentence naming who performs the work and who is accountable for it, and the bid file records the answer given to any question about employment
revisit_triggers: the engagement structure or the supervision arrangement changes
a client says at any point that they believed the cleaners were the broker's own employees

nodes.definition: Whether the people cleaning a building are anyone's employees or independent contractors is a legal question that turns on facts about control and that varies by jurisdiction; it belongs to a qualified professional in the operating jurisdiction and never to a bid deadline. Its role inside acquisition is narrow and concrete: the promises made to win a contract become facts that a later classification review will examine. Language committing the broker to set crew schedules, require uniforms, mandate specific equipment, direct workers task by task on site, guarantee named individuals, or bar a crew from serving other clients is control language, and control is precisely what such reviews weigh. This unit therefore scans every draft proposal and every client demand for that shape of commitment - the right to hire or fire crew members, exclusivity, direct instruction, presenting crew members as broker staff - and routes each flagged item to professional verification before it is written, holding the promise rather than guessing at the wording. It records what was verified, by whom and when, so the same question is not re-answered from memory on the next bid.

included: spotting control-of-worker language in a bid or client demand
routing flagged language to professional verification in the operating jurisdiction
holding the promise until it is cleared
the dated record of what was verified
excluded: the engagement structure decision and the drafting of crew agreements, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base with professional advice
any legal conclusion about a specific arrangement
jurisdiction-specific classification tests stated as settled fact

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a qualified professional in the operating jurisdiction reviews the current arrangement, or a client's demands change the control facts the review would weigh

pros.claim: Catching control language at proposal stage is cheap, while catching it during a dispute or an audit is not
pros.example: replacing a promised clause about the broker's supervisor assigning each cleaner's nightly tasks with an outcome-and-inspection commitment, after a professional review of the wording

cons.claim: Routing wording to professional verification slows bids and sometimes loses a deal to a competitor who promises whatever the client asks for
cons.example: a buyer who wants a named, dedicated, uniformed cleaner written into the agreement and moves on when the broker will not commit before verifying

failure_modes: copying classification-flavored clauses out of another broker's contract because they read professionally
assuming a structure that was fine in one jurisdiction transfers to the next city or state
treating a client's demand for direct control of workers as a commercial detail rather than a flagged question
acceptance_tests: every proposal is scanned for control-of-worker language before it is sent, and each flagged clause carries a dated record of the professional verification that cleared it or of the decision to leave it out
revisit_triggers: the broker bids in a new jurisdiction
a client demands direction, exclusivity or named-individual commitments over crew members

nodes.definition: Commercial buyers are not only buying cleaning; they are buying evidence that somebody's insurance stands behind people who will hold keys to their building. The obligation classes that recur in this trade are recognizable - general liability, a janitorial or fidelity bond class covering theft by service workers, workers' compensation for whoever employs the labor, auto liability where vehicles are used, umbrella limits for larger institutional buyers, additional-insured or certificate-holder status for the client and sometimes the landlord, waiver-of-subrogation language, plus local business licensing and facility-specific requirements such as background-check or badging standards - but the specific limits, forms, endorsements and the question of who must carry each vary by client, facility class, landlord, jurisdiction and year. The work here is to extract those demands from the client's own document before anything is priced, confirm with the broker's agent and the crew side which are genuinely held today, carry the cost of any gap into the price build, and never write that a certificate or endorsement exists before it has been issued.

included: enumerating the requirement classes named in each opportunity's own documents
confirming with the broker's agent what is actually in force
pricing the cost of closing a gap
certificate timing relative to the service start date
excluded: advice on whether any coverage is adequate, or reading a policy on a client's behalf, which is a professional's work
the crew-side coverage verification workflow, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
stated limits, premiums or bond amounts presented as typical for the trade

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a client's vendor-requirement document, a landlord's rules or the broker's own policy terms change what must be evidenced

pros.claim: Pulling certificate demands before pricing prevents both classic losses: bidding a job whose required coverage costs more than the spread, and winning a job that cannot legally start
pros.example: a clinic requiring additional-insured status and a bond class the broker does not yet hold, discovered while pricing rather than in the week before the start date

cons.claim: Requirement classes move, so re-verification consumes time on every bid including repeat clients and renewals
cons.example: a landlord that updates its vendor insurance requirements mid-term, so a bid for a second suite in the same building must be re-checked from scratch

failure_modes: assuming last year's certificate package satisfies this client's document
quoting before checking whether the required limits are obtainable and at what cost
writing fully bonded and insured into a proposal without the specific classes confirmed behind it
acceptance_tests: each bid file lists the coverage, bonding and licensing classes taken from the client's own document, the date each was confirmed with the broker's agent, and the cost of any gap carried into the price build
revisit_triggers: the client, the landlord or the facility class changes its vendor requirements
the broker's own policy renews or the carrier changes terms or endorsements

nodes.definition: Write down how contracts may and may not be won before there is a pipeline, so the rules are not re-decided in a slow month. Four constraints bind this trade. No fear-selling: health, infection, pest, liability and inspection risks may be described only as factual conditions actually observed during the walkthrough, stated once and in writing, never escalated into a scare narrative to force a decision. No bait pricing: a number is never quoted below the cost build with the intent of raising it once the client is captive or the incumbent has been released. No unevidenced disparagement: the broker describes what its own system does, and where a client volunteers a failure it addresses that failure class, without inventing stories about a competitor's staff or conduct. And care proportional to buyer sophistication: a solo practice owner, a volunteer board treasurer or a first-time franchisee gets the scope, exclusions, term and cancellation walked through in plain language with time to read, while a professional facilities department may be sold to at its own pace. The unit also names the pressure situations in which these constraints usually fail - a month with a revenue gap, a rival's implausible number, a buyer who invites exaggeration - because that is when they have to hold.

included: the four selling constraints
the plain-language duty scaled to buyer sophistication
the named pressure situations where constraints fail
excluded: complaint handling and retention behavior on live accounts, owned by the retention knowledge base
crew conduct standards inside client buildings, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
marketing copy production and channel selection

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a buyer reports feeling pressured or surprised by a term, or a rival's tactic creates internal pressure to relax one of the constraints

pros.claim: Constraints written in advance survive a bad month far better than intentions held in the moment
pros.example: a broker three weeks into a slow quarter still declining to send a below-cost number to a hesitating retail buyer because the no-bait rule and the walk-away floor are already on paper

cons.claim: The constraints cost visible near-term wins against competitors who use urgency and scare framing
cons.example: losing a small clinic to a bidder who warns about inspection failures and quotes an implausibly low monthly price

failure_modes: treating a factual observation as a licence to escalate it into a warning campaign
explaining terms quickly to an unsophisticated buyer and calling that disclosure
quoting a capture-now-raise-later number when the month is short
acceptance_tests: the constraint list is written and dated, and every proposal to a low-sophistication buyer records that scope, exclusions, term and cancellation were walked through in plain language before signature
revisit_triggers: a salesperson, referral partner or subcontracted seller is added to the acquisition path
a lost bid produces internal pressure to match a rival's fear-based pitch

nodes.definition: Offices, medical and dental clinics, retail units and industrial or warehouse space are not four sizes of the same job; they differ along the variables that drive every number later in the bid. Soil and traffic load differ (a warehouse floor and a partitioned law office age and soil in completely different ways). Fixture density differs, and restrooms are the most labor-dense element in most commercial buildings, so stall, urinal and sink counts matter more than raw area in clinics, gyms and public-facing retail. Floor mix differs - broadloom carpet, resilient tile that wants burnishing or periodic refinishing, sealed concrete, ceramic - and each carries different nightly and periodic labor. Access windows differ sharply: an after-hours office, a retail store cleaned before opening, a clinic cleaned between patient blocks and a plant running three shifts impose different crew availability problems. And each class carries a compliance overlay - clinical waste handling and exam-room protocols, food-adjacent retail rules, industrial safety inductions and badging - whose specifics are obligation classes verified per site rather than assumed from the class. The unit produces a written profile per class the broker can actually serve given its crew supply and equipment reality, so a walkthrough verifies expectations instead of discovering them.

included: per-class soil, fixture, floor, access and compliance profiles
which classes the broker can serve today given crews and equipment
class-driven risk flags carried into scoping
excluded: the specific scope of an individual site, which is built at the walkthrough
recruiting crews with the skills a class needs, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
any claim about a class's typical profitability stated as a figure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: delivered hours from won contracts in a class contradict the drivers the profile assumed

pros.claim: A class profile tells the broker what will dominate the labor load before it ever enters the building, so the walkthrough confirms rather than improvises
pros.example: knowing before arrival that a dental suite's operatory count and clinical waste handling, not its floor area, will drive the hours and the compliance questions

cons.claim: Class-level generalization hides large within-class variation and can anchor a bid to the wrong archetype
cons.example: treating a seven-day fitness-adjacent retail unit like a nine-to-five boutique of identical footprint and pricing the same nightly hours

failure_modes: chasing a facility class the broker cannot staff or equip today
carrying an office production mindset into a medical or industrial bid
leaving the access window unexamined until it collapses the crew plan after the win
acceptance_tests: each pursued class has a written profile naming its soil, fixture, floor and access drivers and its compliance-class flags, and the broker records whether crews and equipment for that class are actually available
revisit_triggers: the broker enters a facility class it has not bid before
crew or equipment availability for a class changes in a territory

nodes.definition: Map, per opportunity, who signs, who influences, what kind of process governs, and when a decision is actually possible. In small offices and clinics the decision usually sits with an owner, practice administrator or office manager who buys on trust and responsiveness and can decide in one meeting. In multi-tenant or institutional property the buyer is a property or facilities manager who buys on documentation, insurance compliance, references and a formal bid, and who may be scored by a procurement function that weights price heavily. In retail a store manager may host the walkthrough while a regional or corporate agreement actually governs. In industrial sites operations or safety staff hold a veto over anything touching production or safety access. Two timing mechanisms matter more than any pitch: the contract anniversary and its notice requirement, since most commercial cleaning agreements renew or terminate on written notice and the window to be present is before that notice date rather than after it, which is why a pipeline in this business is a calendar rather than a list; and the trigger event - a failed inspection, a building sale, a new manager, an expansion, a complaint that reached an owner - which opens a window outside the anniversary. The unit records the signer, the influencers, the process type and the next real window with the date it was learned and from whom.

included: decision roles by facility class
relationship sale versus formal bid process type
anniversary and notice timing plus trigger events
the pipeline maintained as a calendar
excluded: renewal and repricing conversations on the broker's own live accounts, owned by the retention knowledge base
crew scheduling and shift planning
any claim about typical sales-cycle length or close rate stated as a figure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: win and loss records show bids arriving outside the real decision window or aimed at a role that could not decide

pros.claim: Knowing the notice window turns prospecting from cold interruption into arriving at the moment a change is actually possible
pros.example: meeting a facilities manager whose current agreement requires written notice before its anniversary two months before that date rather than a week after it has auto-extended

cons.claim: Mapping roles and timing is slow work that produces no revenue until a window opens, and the people mapped move on
cons.example: a carefully mapped office manager who leaves for another employer and takes the whole relationship history with her

failure_modes: pitching the person who hosts the walkthrough but cannot sign anything
arriving after the renewal notice date has already extended the incumbent for another term
treating a formal scored bid like a relationship sale and being eliminated on documentation
acceptance_tests: each opportunity record names the signer, the influencers, the process type and the next decision window, each with the date it was learned and the person it came from
revisit_triggers: the site's decision-maker changes role or employer
a mapped opportunity turns out to run as a formal scored bid rather than a relationship sale

nodes.definition: A contract's delivered cost is not confined to what happens inside the building. Crew travel between stops, the willingness of a crew to accept a single isolated site, the broker's own drive time for inspections and complaint visits, and the physical possibility of covering a no-show from a nearby account are all functions of how tightly the book clusters. A site inside an existing cluster can often be staffed by an already-committed crew at a marginal cost, inspected on a route that already exists, and backfilled the same evening from fifteen minutes away. An isolated site far from any cluster is priced by whoever is willing to drive there, is inspected only by a dedicated trip, and has no reachable backup when a crew fails. This unit therefore treats geography as a bid variable rather than a logistics afterthought: it maps the current clusters, marks the outer edge of the serviceable radius for each, and forces a decision before scoping about whether an out-of-cluster site is a deliberate anchor for a new cluster - priced with its real travel and inspection cost, and honestly, rather than as if it sat downtown - or simply a margin leak dressed as growth.

included: cluster mapping and serviceable radius
marginal versus isolated staffing cost
inspection and backfill reachability
the deliberate anchor decision for a new area
excluded: recruiting crews and building coverage in a new territory, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
inspection execution and cadence once live, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
routing software selection and route optimization mechanics

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: actual inspection and backfill trips to an outlying account reveal costs the cluster assumption never priced

pros.claim: Clustering converts one crew's travel into several billable stops and makes same-night backup coverage physically possible
pros.example: three offices in one business park served on a single route, where a cleaner calling in sick is covered from a site a few minutes away

cons.claim: Density discipline blocks otherwise attractive contracts and can stall entry into a new area entirely
cons.example: declining a well-paying clinic twenty-five miles out because no crew and no backup exist there and the anchor decision was not taken

failure_modes: pricing an isolated site as if it sat inside the cluster
taking an anchor site and then never building the cluster it was meant to seed
leaving inspection and complaint drive time out of the cost build for outlying accounts
acceptance_tests: every bid records whether the site sits inside an existing cluster, and out-of-cluster bids state either the added travel and inspection cost carried into the price or an explicit, dated anchor decision
revisit_triggers: a cluster loses the account that anchored it
crew availability appears or disappears in a territory

nodes.definition: The walkthrough is the expensive step, so a screen decides whether to spend it. Before scheduling, the broker establishes: who can actually sign and whether that person will be present; whether a budget exists at all, evidenced by a current provider being paid or a stated intent to begin service; what the real dissatisfaction is, which may be price, quality, communication, turnover, or simply a manager who needs three quotes to justify renewing the incumbent; the access window and any badging or security requirement; the insurance, bonding and licensing classes named in the client's own documents; whether crews plausibly exist for that geography and that access window; whatever payment-behavior signal is available, since a building known for paying vendors late is a margin problem no price fixes; and whether the buyer is shopping on price alone. A recorded no-bid is a legitimate outcome, and so is a conditional bid offered only if the scope is written the broker's way. The output is a dated screening record whose reasons later become the evidence for tuning the screen itself against what actually happened to the accounts that passed it.

included: signer, budget, dissatisfaction, access, requirement-class and staffability screening
payment-behavior signals
the recorded no-bid and the conditional bid
excluded: the site walkthrough itself
recruiting crews to make an unstaffable site staffable, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
formal credit assessment or credit reporting on a prospect

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: win-loss outcomes and the first months of screened-in accounts show which screen questions actually predicted a good contract

pros.claim: One screening conversation kills the bids that would otherwise cost a walkthrough, a full scope build and a proposal to lose
pros.example: learning by phone that the manager needs a third quote purely to justify renewing the incumbent at a lower price

cons.claim: A screen tuned too tight discards winnable business, particularly from buyers who answer questions badly on the telephone
cons.example: dropping a small manufacturer whose owner is monosyllabic by phone but decisive and loyal in person

failure_modes: walking sites for buyers who only need a comparison quote
screening for enthusiasm rather than for authority, budget and staffability
skipping the crew-supply question and winning a site nobody can staff
acceptance_tests: each opportunity has a dated screening record naming the signer, the budget signal, the requirement classes, the staffability answer and an explicit bid or no-bid decision with its reason
revisit_triggers: the win rate of screened-in bids moves materially in either direction
no-bid decisions start being overridden informally in slow months

nodes.definition: Almost every commercial building already has a cleaner, so most contracts are displacements, and the diagnosis of why the incumbent is failing decides both whether the bid is winnable and whether it is worth winning. Four failure classes behave differently. Price: the client wants the same service for less, the least defensible win because the same logic will be used against the broker at its own renewal. Quality: the work genuinely is not being done, where the first question is whether a written scope ever existed, since an unwritten scope makes every provider look like a failure. Communication: the cleaning is adequate but nobody answers the phone or closes the loop, the class a broker with a real inspection and response system can beat honestly and durably. Turnover and instability: constant new faces, missed nights, no backup - a class the broker must be certain it will not reproduce with its own crew arrangement. The read also detects two traps: an incumbent priced below any sustainable cost build, which usually means under-servicing, unpaid labor or a scope far thinner than the client believes; and the chronically dissatisfied site, where expectations exceed anything a frequency matrix can deliver and the next provider will fail exactly as the last one did.

included: the four failure classes and what each implies for scope and price
the below-cost incumbent trap
the chronic-complainer site
checking whether a written scope ever existed
excluded: repeating or inventing unverified stories about a competitor
handling complaints on the broker's own accounts once live, owned by the retention knowledge base
crew quality scoring mechanics, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: complaint patterns in the first months after a displacement win show whether the diagnosed failure class was the real one

pros.claim: Naming the failure class tells the broker what to sell and what to price instead of reflexively discounting
pros.example: a client whose real complaint is that nobody returns calls, won on a written response commitment and an inspection report rather than on a lower monthly number

cons.claim: Clients misreport their own dissatisfaction, so the read can be confidently wrong and shape the whole bid around a fiction
cons.example: a manager who says the problem is quality when the instruction from above was simply to cut the facilities budget

failure_modes: matching a below-cost incumbent price and inheriting an unsustainable job
taking a chronic-complainer site because its budget looks attractive
building the entire pitch on the incumbent's faults rather than on the broker's own system
acceptance_tests: the bid file names the incumbent failure class, the evidence behind that diagnosis, and whether the client's existing written scope, if any, actually covered the disputed work
revisit_triggers: the walkthrough contradicts the complaint the client described by phone
a won displacement produces the same complaints within its first weeks

nodes.definition: The walkthrough is the only step that converts a building into data, so it runs as a protocol rather than a tour. The broker walks every space that will be cleaned and records: area by space type; floor surface by area; restroom count with fixture counts, since stalls, urinals and sinks concentrate labor more than any other element; kitchens and break rooms with the dish, appliance and stocking expectations attached to them; entrances, matting and glass; trash volume, container count and the physical haul path to the dumpster, because a long haul is labor; occupancy and headcount; obstruction, meaning cubicle density, desk clutter, stacked stock and equipment on floors, which is what makes a borrowed production rate wrong; access reality including keys, alarm codes, badging, elevator use and the hours the building is truly available; the janitorial closet, water source and storage; and the client's own expectations, written down verbatim as they are spoken. The visit is also where buyer sophistication and the incumbent's real failure become visible. Nothing is quoted on the spot: the protocol ends with a confirmation of scope and a promise of a written proposal, never with a number spoken across a hallway.

included: the room-by-room capture list
fixture, floor, obstruction, trash-haul and access observation
client expectations recorded verbatim
the rule against quoting during the visit
excluded: quoting a price on site
the recurring inspection walkthroughs of live accounts, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
the crew's operational site orientation, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a scope dispute or a crew report reveals a capture item the protocol does not currently collect

pros.claim: A protocol makes the bid reproducible and defensible, because every number in the price build traces to something observed and dated
pros.example: a scope argument in month two settled by the walkthrough record noting that the client asked for the break-room refrigerator to be excluded

cons.claim: A thorough walkthrough consumes real time on a site that may never be won, and buyers often try to compress it
cons.example: a store manager who allots fifteen minutes between deliveries for a unit that needs an hour to capture properly

failure_modes: quoting on the spot in order to look decisive
walking only the areas the client chooses to show
recording impressions instead of counts, so the labor model has nothing to stand on
acceptance_tests: the walkthrough record contains area by space type, floor mix, fixture counts, obstruction notes, the trash-haul path, access constraints and the client's verbatim expectations, each dated and attributed
revisit_triggers: the client changes the space, occupancy or operating hours before signature
crew reports after the win contradict the recorded site conditions

nodes.definition: The number that drives the entire labor model is cleanable square footage by surface type - the area a crew actually cleans - and it is not the leased or gross figure a client reads off a lease, which includes walls, shafts, unfinished storage, common areas billed to other tenants and space the crew never enters. This unit establishes that number by measuring or by marking up a floor plan, splits it by surface (carpet, resilient tile, sealed concrete, ceramic, wood, rubber), separates restrooms and kitchens because they are computed on fixture counts rather than area, and records explicitly which areas are out of scope. It also records the periodic-work surfaces separately, since the tile that will need burnishing or refinishing and the carpet that will need extraction generate a different cost line than nightly service. Every figure carries how it was obtained - walked and measured, taken from a plan, or supplied by the client - because a client-supplied number is a hypothesis rather than a measurement, and an area error does not appear once: it repeats in every month of the contract at the same proportion.

included: cleanable versus gross area
the surface-type split
restroom and kitchen separation for fixture-based computation
explicitly excluded areas
provenance of every figure
excluded: the crew's own verification of area after starting, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
floor-care technique and product selection
assumed area-per-hour figures, which belong to the production rate model

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a re-measure or delivered crew time contradicts the recorded cleanable area or surface split

pros.claim: Measuring cleanable area removes the single largest source of bid error and the one that compounds every month of the term
pros.example: a lease-stated footprint that includes a mezzanine storage area and a shared lobby the crew will never touch

cons.claim: Measuring costs time and some clients will not release a plan or allow a second visit
cons.example: a tenant who declines to share the floor plan and offers only the square footage printed in the lease

failure_modes: pricing from the client's leased-area figure without marking it as unverified
recording one blended area with no surface split, so periodic work cannot be costed
failing to list excluded areas, which the client later assumes were included
acceptance_tests: the bid file states cleanable area by surface type with the provenance of each figure and an explicit list of excluded areas
revisit_triggers: the client alters the space or takes an additional suite before signature
crew-reported time on a comparable route suggests the measured area is wrong

nodes.definition: Write the scope as a matrix - each task, in each area, at a stated frequency - because that matrix is simultaneously the thing being priced, the instruction the crew will receive, and the standard against which every future complaint is judged. Nightly and weekly tasks (trash removal, restroom service and restocking, vacuuming, mopping, spot cleaning, entrance glass, touchpoint disinfection) sit in one band; weekly-to-monthly detail tasks (edge vacuuming, high dusting, vent grilles, baseboards, partition wipe-down) in another; periodic tasks (carpet extraction, hard-floor burnishing, strip and refinish, interior and exterior windows, upholstery) in a third, separated deliberately so they cannot hide inside a nightly price. Equally important is the exclusion list, written explicitly rather than implied: dishes left in sinks, personal desk surfaces, biohazard or bodily-fluid cleanup beyond ordinary restroom service, exterior grounds, high-access glass, tenant-owned equipment, snow and ice, pest control, and any consumable the client supplies. Unwritten scope is never free - it is the exact mechanism by which a healthy contract becomes a losing one, because anything a client believes is included will eventually be demanded, performed unpaid, or turned into a complaint that costs more than the work.

included: the task by area by frequency matrix
the three frequency bands
the explicit exclusion list
a written statement of who supplies consumables
excluded: the crew-facing scope handoff pack and training on it, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
managing scope creep on live accounts, owned by the retention knowledge base
cleaning technique and product specification

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: post-award disputes or repeated extra-work requests show tasks the matrix never named

pros.claim: A matrix ends the argument about what was included before it starts and gives the crew an instruction rather than an impression
pros.example: an explicit line stating that break-room dishes are excluded, agreed at bid time instead of argued about in month two

cons.claim: A dense matrix can read as bureaucratic to a small buyer and takes real time to build for every bid, won or lost
cons.example: a two-page scope annex for a small suite whose owner expected a one-paragraph quote by email

failure_modes: verbal promises made during the walkthrough that never enter the matrix
omitting the exclusion list because it feels negative in a sales document
burying periodic work inside the nightly band so its cost never appears
acceptance_tests: every priced task appears in the matrix with an area and a frequency, the exclusion list is present, and the consumables responsibility is stated in writing
revisit_triggers: the client requests a task that does not appear in the matrix
an extra-work authorization reveals a gap the matrix never covered

nodes.definition: The labor load is the engine of the bid, and it is arithmetic rather than intuition: for each task and space type, hours equal the measured area, or the fixture count, divided by a production rate - the area or fixture volume one worker completes per hour at the required standard - adjusted for obstruction and then multiplied by frequency to give hours per week and per month. Restrooms and kitchens are computed on fixture counts rather than area; day-porter coverage is computed as staffed hours rather than by rate; periodic work is computed on its own line and amortized across the year rather than folded into nightly hours. The honest part of this unit is where the rates come from: published industry rate references, quotes from crews who have done comparable buildings, or best of all the broker's own timed observation of its crews performing the same task in a comparable space, with every rate carrying its source and its uncertainty. Rates are not constants - obstruction, soil load, equipment (a wide-area machine versus an upright vacuum), building layout and worker experience all move them - so the model is maintained as a source-tagged rate library that delivered hours continuously correct, never as a fixed number lifted from a competitor's spreadsheet and presented as an industry standard.

included: the hours arithmetic per task and space type
fixture-based computation for restrooms and kitchens
the obstruction adjustment
the source-tagged rate library
periodic hours computed separately
excluded: crew scheduling and shift construction, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
any production rate presented as an industry-standard fact
equipment purchasing decisions and their financing

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: timed observation of the broker's own crews replaces or corrects a borrowed production rate in the library

pros.claim: Explicit labor arithmetic makes a bid auditable, so when delivered hours disagree the error can be located instead of guessed at
pros.example: tracing a monthly overrun to a restroom line that assumed one sink where the site actually has three

cons.claim: Rates carry genuine uncertainty, and a confident model propagates a wrong rate into every line that uses it
cons.example: an open-plan carpet rate applied unchanged to a heavily partitioned suite where the crew cannot run a straight pass

failure_modes: using one blended rate across all surfaces and space types
omitting the obstruction adjustment so the crew needs more time than the bid pays for
leaving periodic work inside the nightly hours where its cost disappears
acceptance_tests: the labor worksheet shows per-task hours with the rate used, that rate's source, the obstruction adjustment and the frequency multiplier, and periodic hours appear on their own line
revisit_triggers: delivered crew hours diverge from bid hours on comparable sites
equipment, required standard or crew experience changes on a route

nodes.definition: Hours become cost through a build that must contain everything the broker will actually pay or absorb, in the structure the engagement actually uses. Where crews are engaged as subcontracted firms, the labor line is their quoted price for the written scope - quoted against the matrix, never against a verbal description of the building - plus whatever the arrangement leaves with the broker. Where labor is employed, the build carries wage plus the employer burden classes, meaning payroll taxes, workers' compensation, paid-time policies and any benefits, whose rates and applicability are jurisdiction-specific and verified rather than assumed, with the classification question itself held as a flagged professional matter rather than decided inside a spreadsheet. On top of the labor line sit the costs bids habitually forget: consumables and supplies where the contract assigns them to the broker, equipment provision, wear and replacement, travel and inspection trips, periodic work whether subcontracted or self-performed, the cost of backfilling a missed night, billing and collection effort, and an allowance for the complaint-response time this particular account will consume. The output is a monthly delivered cost for this specific site, assembled from quotes and measured inputs, with each line tagged by whether it is quoted, measured or estimated.

included: subcontracted price line versus employed-labor build
burden classes flagged for jurisdictional verification
supplies, equipment, travel, inspection, backfill, billing and complaint allowances
per-line source tagging
excluded: negotiating crew rates and selecting which crew gets the work, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
the classification determination itself, which is a professional's decision
any wage, burden percentage or supply cost stated as a market figure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the first months of crew payments and supplier invoices show a cost class the build under-stated or omitted

pros.claim: A build that names every absorbed cost prevents the common failure of a spread that looks healthy until the first backfill and the first supply order
pros.example: a bid whose apparent margin evaporates once the broker's own paper-goods obligation and the monthly inspection drive are entered as lines

cons.claim: Some cost classes such as backfill frequency and complaint time can only be estimated at bid time, and those estimates are weakest for a first contract in a new class
cons.example: a first industrial site where nobody yet knows how often a crew will need covering on a third shift

failure_modes: pricing against a verbal crew quote rather than a quote given against the written matrix
omitting consumables, equipment or inspection travel because they feel like overhead
assuming burden classes and rates from another jurisdiction or another year
acceptance_tests: the cost build lists every cost line with its source - crew quote, supplier quote, measured input or flagged estimate - and totals a monthly delivered cost for this site
revisit_triggers: a crew requotes or a supplier changes consumable pricing
actual backfill or complaint effort on comparable accounts exceeds the allowance used

nodes.definition: Price is built rather than guessed: delivered cost plus a retained spread, presented as the monthly recurring amount the client will actually see, with per-square-foot or per-hour equivalents used only as internal sanity checks and never as a headline claim about what cleaning costs. The discipline lies in naming what the spread has to fund before judging whether it is enough - the acquisition effort that won this account, administration and billing, the inspections the proposal promises, the response commitment being made, the risk of paid backfill when a crew fails, bad debt, the insurance and bonding carried at broker level, and only then profit. A spread expressed as a fixed monthly amount and a spread expressed as a percentage of price behave differently as a contract ages: the fixed amount erodes silently as crew cost rises, while the percentage holds only if the price itself can move. This unit therefore ties the price to the repricing mechanism that will appear in the contract terms, and emits both the number and the assumption set behind it in a form the renewal conversation can read a year later without reconstructing anything.

included: cost-plus-spread construction
the list of what the spread funds
monthly price presentation with internal per-foot and per-hour checks
the link between price and the repricing clause
excluded: monthly margin monitoring, drift detection and mid-term repricing conversations, owned by the retention knowledge base
crew payment negotiation, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
any spread percentage, price point or per-foot rate asserted as typical

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: delivered cost data or a repricing event shows the spread did not fund what it was supposed to fund

pros.claim: Pricing from a named cost stack means a discount request can be answered with what would have to change, rather than with a shrug or a silent concession
pros.example: answering a request for a lower number by showing the frequency reduction or scope change that would produce it

cons.claim: Cost-plus pricing leaves value uncaptured where a client would pay more for reliability, and prices the broker out where a rival under-costs the same building
cons.example: losing a bid to a competitor whose monthly number sits below the broker's own delivered cost line

failure_modes: setting price from what the incumbent charges instead of from the cost build
committing to a fixed monthly amount with no repricing mechanism behind it
quoting a per-square-foot number to a client as though it were a market rate
acceptance_tests: the price build shows the delivered cost, the spread, what that spread funds, and the monthly price, with the assumptions register attached to it
revisit_triggers: crew or supply cost moves between the bid and signature
the client requests a scope or frequency change during negotiation

nodes.definition: Before the price is spoken aloud, test it against the ways its inputs could be wrong, because a bid is a long commitment made on one visit's evidence. The tests are specific and each maps to a real mechanism: what happens to the spread if cleanable area proves materially larger than measured; if the production rate was optimistic and delivered hours run longer; if the crew requotes upward at the first renewal of its own arrangement; if the client adds a frequency or a task without paying for it; if backfill is needed more often than the allowance assumed; if payment runs slow enough to matter. Out of those tests comes the walk-away floor - the price below which this site will not be bid - fixed and dated before any price conversation rather than produced under pressure inside one, together with the non-price concessions permitted instead: a start date, a payment term, a scope trade, a phased frequency, a shorter initial term. The paired skill is losing on purpose and recording the loss with its price and reason, so that the pattern of near-misses becomes evidence about the rate library and the cost build rather than an argument for panic discounting.

included: input sensitivity tests tied to real mechanisms
the dated walk-away floor set before negotiation
permitted non-price concessions
recorded-loss discipline
excluded: repricing or exiting a live contract that has already gone bad, owned by the retention knowledge base
renegotiating crew rates, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
competitor price intelligence presented as fact

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: won and lost bid outcomes show the floor was set on an assumption band the delivered data contradicts

pros.claim: A floor decided in advance turns a negotiation into a comparison against a number that already exists instead of an emotional moment
pros.example: answering a buyer's meet-this-and-it-is-yours with a scope-reduced alternative rather than a below-floor yes

cons.claim: Sensitivity work adds a step to every bid, and the assumed error bands are themselves judgments that can be too narrow
cons.example: a broker whose assumed area-error band is far too tight for a site whose footprint came off a plan rather than a tape

failure_modes: setting the floor during the meeting rather than before it
conceding price when a scope or frequency concession was available
discarding lost-bid data so the pattern in the losses is never learned
acceptance_tests: each bid file contains the sensitivity results, a stated walk-away floor with its date, and the list of non-price concessions that are permitted
revisit_triggers: several losses cluster just above the floor, suggesting the cost build or the rate library is off
a delivered account breaches an assumption the sensitivity test relied on

nodes.definition: Periodic work - carpet extraction, hard-floor burnishing, strip and refinish, window cleaning, pressure washing, post-construction cleanup, upholstery, high dusting - behaves nothing like nightly service: it runs on cycles, often needs specialist equipment or a specialist crew, and consumes hours in a lump rather than a trickle. Burying it inside the monthly recurring price is the quiet mechanism by which a healthy contract turns into a losing one, because the client hears the word included and the broker meets the cost when the cycle comes due. The disciplined construction gives each periodic service its own line with its own cycle and price, presented in one of three honest ways: excluded from the monthly and quoted per event; included at a stated cycle written into the matrix with its cost amortized into the monthly build; or offered as an optional line the client may add later. Consumables and supplies get the same treatment - who buys paper, liners, soap and can liners is a priced decision, not an assumption anyone should have to discover. At bid time this is purely margin protection; using these same lines to grow an account over its life belongs to the downstream expansion work, not here.

included: separate line pricing for each periodic service
the three honest presentations of periodic work
amortization when a cycle is included
consumables responsibility as a priced decision
excluded: selling add-ons and expanding accounts over the contract life, owned by the retention knowledge base
sourcing specialist crews and equipment for periodic work, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
any per-event price presented as typical for the trade

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the real cost of an executed periodic cycle differs from the amortized allowance carried in the build

pros.claim: Separate lines make periodic cost visible to both sides and remove the surprise that otherwise arrives with the first refinishing cycle
pros.example: a strip-and-refinish cycle quoted as its own event with its own price rather than assumed inside a monthly number

cons.claim: Itemized lines can make an honest proposal look more expensive than a rival's single bundled figure
cons.example: losing a side-by-side comparison to a one-line monthly price that silently excludes all floor care

failure_modes: writing that floor care is included with no cycle stated
including a cycle without amortizing its cost into the monthly build
leaving the consumables question unanswered in the proposal
acceptance_tests: every periodic service appears with its cycle and its price treatment, and the consumables responsibility is stated in writing in the proposal
revisit_triggers: a client requests a periodic service that was not in the proposal
equipment or specialist crew cost for a periodic service changes materially

nodes.definition: The proposal is written to be read by three audiences at once: the buyer deciding today, the crew that will later receive the scope, and the broker's own future self at the first complaint or the first renewal. It therefore carries the task-and-frequency matrix as an annex rather than adjectives about quality; the exclusion list; the monthly price with periodic and optional lines shown separately; the service-model disclosure sentence; the insurance and bonding classes the broker will evidence with certificates, named as classes and produced as documents rather than asserted as limits before they are confirmed; the start and transition plan covering keys, alarm codes, access, badging and the first week's schedule; the inspection and communication commitment with a named contact and a response commitment the broker can genuinely meet; and references the buyer is invited to call. The governing writing rule is that every claim must be verifiable, contractual, or absent - no hospital-grade language without a substantiated basis, no fully bonded and insured without the certificate classes behind it, no promised staffing pattern the crew arrangement cannot actually deliver, and no green or health claim the broker cannot support if asked.

included: scope annex and exclusions
priced lines including periodic and optional work
the disclosure sentence
certificate classes to be evidenced
transition plan
inspection and response commitment
references
excluded: the internal cost build and crew pricing, which are never shown to the client
the crew-facing scope handoff pack, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
ongoing service reporting to the client once live, owned by the retention knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a post-award dispute or a gap found at crew handoff reveals a section the proposal template omits

pros.claim: One document that the client, the crew and the renewal conversation all read from removes the drift between what was sold and what is delivered
pros.example: an inspection commitment written into the proposal that both the crew handoff and the first complaint response refer back to

cons.claim: A complete proposal takes longer to produce than a one-page quote, and some buyers reward speed over substance
cons.example: a manager who awards the contract to whoever emailed a number the same afternoon as the walkthrough

failure_modes: unverifiable superlatives standing in for a scope annex
promising a response time nobody is staffed or rostered to meet
sending a price with no exclusion list attached to it
acceptance_tests: the proposal contains the scope annex, the exclusions, the priced lines, the disclosure sentence, the certificate classes and the transition plan, and every service claim in it traces to something contractual or documented
revisit_triggers: a client asks for a claim or guarantee the broker cannot evidence
the crew handoff reveals a proposal commitment the crew arrangement cannot support

nodes.definition: These are the clause classes that decide whether a well-built bid survives a year of operations, each mapped to the margin mechanism it protects. Term length and renewal mechanism, and what notice each requires. The cancellation notice each side may give, and whether it is symmetric. A price-adjustment mechanism tied to a stated cause - labor cost changes, statutory wage changes, supply cost, added area or increased occupancy - because without one, every cost rise is silently absorbed by the spread. An extra-work authorization requiring written approval before unscoped work is performed, which is the clause that converts scope creep from a loss into a line item. Holiday and closure handling. Consumables and equipment responsibility. Access, keys, alarm and security duties and what happens when access fails through no fault of the crew. Damage, liability and indemnity allocation. Payment terms, late handling and suspension rights. Non-solicitation of the broker's crews by the client. Assignment on sale of the building. And the insurance and bonding evidence obligations flowing both ways. Every one of these is a CLASS whose customary form and enforceability vary by jurisdiction and by whose paper is used; the broker's job is to know which clause protects which mechanism and to have a qualified professional draft and review the document, never to practise law on its own contract.

included: the clause classes and the margin mechanism each protects
the choice of whose paper governs
what must not be signed without professional review
excluded: legal drafting, interpretation, or any assertion that a clause is enforceable in a jurisdiction
renewal negotiation and mid-term repricing conversations, owned by the retention knowledge base
crew-side agreements and their terms, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a live contract meets a cost or scope event its clause set never anticipated, or a professional review changes the broker's standard clause set

pros.claim: A price-adjustment mechanism and a written extra-work rule are the two clauses that most often decide whether a contract's second year is profitable
pros.example: a wage-driven cost increase that can be raised with the client because the agreement already named that cause

cons.claim: Insisting on protective clauses loses deals with institutional buyers whose procurement paper is genuinely non-negotiable
cons.example: a corporate vendor agreement fixing price for a multi-year term while reserving unilateral scope-change rights

failure_modes: signing the client's paper unread because the price was already agreed
having no extra-work clause, so every unscoped request becomes free work
accepting an asymmetric cancellation notice without noticing the asymmetry
acceptance_tests: the agreement is checked against the clause-class list before signature, every gap is recorded, and anything the broker cannot accept is negotiated or escalated to a qualified professional before signing
revisit_triggers: the client requires its own procurement paper instead of the broker's
a cost cause arises that the price-adjustment clause does not name

nodes.definition: With truthful disclosure in the proposal and a floor under the price, what is left to compete on is the part of the service a buyer cannot see in a quote: what happens when something goes wrong. Honest differentiation is assembled entirely from commitments that can be checked - a named contact who actually answers, a stated response commitment for complaints, a written inspection cadence with a report the client receives, a documented backup plan for a crew that fails to appear, a transition plan for the first weeks, references the buyer may call, and a scope annex clear enough that performance can be judged against something. Each of these is a promise the broker's own operations must be able to keep, which is exactly why differentiation is composed after the cost build rather than before it: the inspection visits, the response capacity and the backup arrangement all carry cost that must already be in the price. What it must never be: implied in-house employment, invented certifications, borrowed client lists, eco or medical-grade language with no substantiated basis, or a guarantee of specific named individuals the crew arrangement cannot honour.

included: checkable commitments as the differentiation set
costing each commitment before promising it
the forbidden claim classes
excluded: operating the inspection and complaint systems themselves, owned by the crew sourcing and retention knowledge bases
marketing collateral design and channel strategy
comparative claims about a competitor's staff or conduct

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: delivery data shows a promised inspection cadence or response commitment is not actually being met

pros.claim: Differentiating on the response system attacks exactly the failure class most incumbents lose accounts on, without touching price
pros.example: winning a communication-failure account on a written response commitment and a named contact rather than on a lower monthly number

cons.claim: Every checkable promise becomes an operational obligation with a cost, and an unmet promise is worse than one never made
cons.example: a promised monthly inspection report that arrives for three months and then quietly stops

failure_modes: promising a response time nobody is rostered to meet
making green or medical-grade claims with no substantiation behind them
differentiating with commitments the crew arrangement cannot support
acceptance_tests: every differentiating claim in the proposal names who delivers it, at what cadence, at what cost already carried in the build, and is checkable by the client
revisit_triggers: an operational failure makes a standing promise untrue
capacity changes so that a committed inspection or response cadence can no longer be met

nodes.definition: Acquisition ends with an artifact rather than a signature. The bid record gathers in one place: the screening decision and its reason; the walkthrough record with dated observations; the measured cleanable area and floor inventory with the provenance of each figure; the task-and-frequency matrix and exclusions as agreed; the labor worksheet with every rate and its source; the cost build with every line tagged quoted, measured or estimated; the price, the spread and the walk-away floor; the sensitivity assumptions; the executed agreement with its clause-class check; the certificate classes evidenced and their dates; and an assumptions register naming every number that was estimated rather than measured. Won or lost, the file is closed the same way, because lost bids carry the price signal that tunes the rate library. On a win it feeds two downstream systems: crew sourcing receives the scope, the hours, the access constraints and the site conditions it must staff against, and margin monitoring receives the cost build and the assumptions register as the baseline it will measure drift from. The governing rule is that nothing has been promised to a client that this record does not contain and the handoff has not been told.

included: the closed bid file's contents
the assumptions register
identical close discipline for wins and losses
what crew sourcing and margin monitoring each receive
excluded: crew selection, onboarding and scope training, owned by the crew sourcing knowledge base
monthly margin tracking, complaint handling and renewal, owned by the retention knowledge base
client-facing service reporting once the account is live

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a downstream crew or margin system reports a missing input that the bid record should have carried forward

pros.claim: A complete record makes the first margin dispute and the first scope argument answerable with evidence instead of memory
pros.example: a month-three complaint resolved by producing the signed matrix and the walkthrough note it came from

cons.claim: Assembling the record costs time at exactly the moment the broker most wants to move on to the next opportunity
cons.example: a win in a busy week filed as a signed contract and a phone number and nothing else

failure_modes: handing the crew a price and an address instead of the scope, hours and constraints
closing without an assumptions register, so later margin drift cannot be attributed to anything
closing lost bids with no price or reason recorded, discarding the only free market signal available
acceptance_tests: the bid record contains every listed element with dates and sources, and both the crew-facing and margin-facing handoffs are produced before the first service night
revisit_triggers: a downstream dispute finds an element missing from the record
margin monitoring cannot attribute a drift because the baseline it received was incomplete

edges.why_related: what must be disclosed follows directly from how the charter says the service is actually delivered and who is accountable for it
which facility classes are worth profiling is decided by the charter's definition of a good contract and its will-not-bid conditions
who signs, on what process and on what cycle differs by facility class, so the class profile precedes the buyer map
the screen tests for the signer, the process type and the decision window that the buyer map defines
the walkthrough is only scheduled for opportunities the screen has passed, because it is the expensive step
cleanable area and the surface split are captured during the walkthrough and cannot be reconstructed afterwards from memory
the matrix is written from what was observed and from the client expectations recorded verbatim on site
the hours arithmetic divides measured area and fixture counts by rates, so the measurement must exist first
hours are computed per task at a stated frequency, so the matrix supplies both the task set and the multipliers
the cost build converts the modelled hours into money, so it cannot precede the labor load
price is delivered cost plus the retained spread, so the cost build is the price build's first term
the walk-away floor is derived by stressing the price build's own inputs, so it needs a finished build to stress
periodic services are priced from the periodic band of the matrix and from the surfaces the inventory identified
the proposal presents the priced lines the price build produced, never a number invented for the document
the agreement formalizes the scope, price and commitments the proposal already made, so the clause work follows the document
the closed bid record includes the executed agreement and its clause-class check, so it cannot close before the terms are settled
the forbidden claim classes and the no-fear-selling rule define the space inside which differentiation may be built
coverage, bonding and licensing the contract requires cost money and must be inside the price before a spread is calculated
whether the labor line is a subcontracted price or a wage-plus-burden build depends on an engagement question that must be verified rather than assumed
clauses granting the client or the broker direction over individual workers are exactly the control facts a classification review examines, so they are held for professional verification
the screen may not qualify an opportunity that can only be won by fear-selling, bait pricing or leaving an unsophisticated buyer uninformed
the proposal must carry the service-model disclosure sentence and may not contain language implying an in-house workforce
an opportunity demanding coverage or bond classes the broker cannot obtain in time is screened out before a walkthrough is spent on it
a site outside any serviceable cluster is either an explicit anchor decision or a no-bid, and the screen is where that is decided
the record cannot be closed without the stated floor and the sensitivity assumptions that margin monitoring will later measure drift against
the pressure to undercut a known incumbent price pulls directly against a price built from this broker's own delivered cost
edges.resolution_rule: the cost-built price and the walk-away floor win; if the incumbent price sits below the floor, respond with a scope or frequency alternative or decline the bid, and never match a number the cost build cannot support

edges.why_related: a buyer who wants more tasks or higher frequency at the same monthly number is asking the spread to absorb labor the matrix has already priced
edges.resolution_rule: scope changes reprice; if the client will not accept a price change, the matrix is reduced by agreement and the reduction is written into the annex before signature, never absorbed silently

edges.why_related: a procurement process scored mainly on price rewards the thinnest compliant bid and gives no points for checkable service commitments
edges.resolution_rule: bid the honest scope and price and let the process score it; where the format allows, attach the checkable commitments as a separate value section, and record a price-scored loss rather than stripping scope to win it

edges.why_related: when the incumbent's failure is blamed on subcontracted labor, the easiest winning story is to imply the broker uses its own employees
edges.resolution_rule: disclosure wins without exception; the broker states its model plainly and competes on the accountability and inspection system rather than on an implied employment structure, even at the cost of the bid

edges.why_related: itemized periodic lines make an honest proposal look dearer than a rival's single bundled monthly figure the buyer is comparing it to
edges.resolution_rule: keep the lines itemized and add a plain comparison note stating what the monthly figure does and does not include, so the buyer can compare like with like; never bundle periodic work into the monthly number without a stated cycle and an amortized cost

edges.why_related: an otherwise attractive institutional opportunity may come with non-negotiable procurement paper that removes the repricing and extra-work protections the margin depends on
edges.resolution_rule: price the removed protection into the bid where the exposure can be quantified, and where it cannot, treat the paper as a screening failure and decline; a professional reviews any clause set the broker has not accepted before

edges.why_related: an area or surface-split error propagates proportionally through hours into cost and repeats in every month of the term
cluster position drives crew travel, inspection trips and backfill feasibility, all of which are cost lines in the build
the diagnosed failure class determines which tasks and frequencies the new matrix must strengthen and which client expectations must be written down explicitly
the incumbent diagnosis is developed after an opportunity survives screening and before the walkthrough, so the visit can test it
the differentiation narrative is written on top of a finished, costed proposal so that every commitment in it is already funded
delivered hours reported back against the recorded bid hours are what correct the source-tagged rate library over time
win, loss and early-account outcomes recorded at close are the only evidence for which screening questions actually predicted a good contract
every extra-work authorization raised under the agreement names a task the matrix failed to cover and should be folded into the next bid's template
