both are obligation classes rather than settled facts: each varies by jurisdiction and contract, must be verified with a qualified professional or the carrier, and is never carried forward by assumption

conflict_axes.name: price_pressure_versus_the_margin_floor
conflict_axes.description: Every displacement bid invites the broker to price against what the client pays today rather than against what this building actually costs to serve.
poles: win the contract at the client's number
hold the price the cost build produced
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the floor and move scope, frequency or start terms instead of price; record the loss with its number so the pattern informs the rate library

conflict_axes.name: walkthrough_generosity_versus_priced_scope
conflict_axes.description: Agreeing to small extra requests during the walkthrough builds rapport but prices nothing, and every unwritten yes becomes unpaid recurring labor.
poles: say yes on site to build the relationship
price only what enters the written matrix
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: welcome the request on site, write it into the matrix, and let it change the number or the exclusion list before signature

conflict_axes.name: borrowed_rates_versus_observed_conditions
conflict_axes.description: A published or borrowed production rate is fast and looks authoritative, while the obstruction, soil load and layout actually seen in the building are slow to quantify but true for this site.
poles: apply the library rate as given
adjust to what the walkthrough observed
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use the library rate as a prior, adjust it by the recorded obstruction and soil observations, tag the source, and let delivered hours correct it

conflict_axes.name: speed_to_quote_versus_scoping_rigor
conflict_axes.description: Buyers frequently reward whoever answers with a number first, while a defensible bid requires measurement the same afternoon cannot produce.
poles: quote fast to stay in the race
measure and scope before quoting
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: commit on site to a delivery date for the written proposal rather than to a number, and keep the no-quote-on-site rule intact

conflict_axes.name: plain_disclosure_versus_competitive_framing
conflict_axes.description: The service model is easier to sell when the buyer is allowed to imagine an in-house crew, and hardest to sell in the exact moment honesty matters most.
poles: let the buyer assume what sells
state the delivery model plainly in writing
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: disclosure is absolute; compete on the accountability and inspection system instead, and accept the bids lost to that discipline

conflict_axes.name: client_control_of_crew_versus_classification_exposure
conflict_axes.description: Clients often want to direct, name, uniform or exclusively reserve the people cleaning their building, and those are precisely the control facts a worker-classification review weighs.
poles: promise the control the client asks for
hold control language until it is professionally verified
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: convert control requests into outcome, inspection and continuity commitments, and route any residual control language to a qualified professional in the operating jurisdiction before it is written

conflict_axes.name: route_density_versus_reach_for_growth
conflict_axes.description: Clustered accounts are cheaper to serve, inspect and backfill, while the attractive contract is often the one outside the cluster.
poles: only bid inside serviceable clusters
reach out to win the better account
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: allow out-of-cluster bids only as explicit, dated anchor decisions with travel, inspection and backfill cost priced in, never as ordinary bids

conflict_axes.name: bundled_simplicity_versus_itemized_honesty
conflict_axes.description: A single monthly figure is easier to compare and easier to sell, but it hides periodic work whose cost arrives in a lump and whose scope the client will assume is included.
poles: present one simple monthly number
itemize periodic and optional lines
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: itemize, then add a plain-language note of what the monthly figure includes and excludes so the buyer can compare competing bids honestly

conflict_axes.name: term_security_versus_repricing_flexibility
conflict_axes.description: A long locked term secures the book but freezes the price against rising crew and supply cost, while a short term keeps flexibility and weakens the account's value.
poles: lock a long term at a fixed price
keep the term short and repriceable
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: prefer a term with a named price-adjustment cause over a shorter term, and never accept a long fixed-price term without a stated adjustment mechanism

conflict_axes.name: client_procurement_paper_versus_broker_protections
conflict_axes.description: Institutional buyers hand over their own vendor agreement, and signing it unchanged is often the price of entry into their portfolio.
poles: sign the client's paper to win the portfolio
hold the protective clause classes
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: quantify and price the removed protections where possible, escalate unfamiliar clause sets to a qualified professional, and decline where the exposure cannot be priced or bounded

edge_cases.description: The buyer supplies a square footage taken from the lease that includes common areas, shafts and unfinished storage the crew will never enter
edge_cases.trigger: a client-supplied area figure is offered in place of a measurement
edge_cases.mitigation: record the figure as client-supplied, measure or mark up a plan before pricing, and if the client refuses access, state the assumed area and its provenance in the proposal so a correction can reprice the contract

edge_cases.description: A medical or dental site carries clinical waste handling, exam-room protocols and training expectations that the broker has never had to satisfy
edge_cases.trigger: a bid in a facility class with a compliance overlay the broker has not served before
edge_cases.mitigation: name the obligation classes, verify current requirements with the relevant authority and the client's own protocol document, price the training and handling, and exclude anything the crew is not qualified to perform

edge_cases.description: The property manager signs and pays, but each tenant behaves as though they are the client and issues instructions to the crew directly
edge_cases.trigger: a multi-tenant building where the payer and the day-to-day requester are different people
edge_cases.mitigation: name the single authorized requester in the agreement, route all scope requests through the extra-work authorization clause, and state in the matrix that tenant-issued instructions are not scope

edge_cases.description: A formal bid is scored almost entirely on price and requires insurance limits and a bid bond above what the broker currently carries
edge_cases.trigger: a procurement-run tender with mandatory financial and coverage thresholds
edge_cases.mitigation: check obtainability and cost of the required classes during screening, price them if obtainable, and record a no-bid with its reason if they are not, rather than bidding and withdrawing after award

edge_cases.description: The incumbent's monthly price sits below the broker's own delivered cost for the same written scope
edge_cases.trigger: a known incumbent price that no honest cost build can reach
edge_cases.mitigation: assume the scopes differ rather than that the rates do, put both scopes side by side for the client, bid the honest scope at the honest price, and decline rather than match

edge_cases.description: The client wants service to start before certificates, access arrangements and the crew handoff are complete
edge_cases.trigger: an incumbent terminated abruptly and the building needs cleaning immediately
edge_cases.mitigation: offer a dated start that the certificate and handoff steps can actually meet, or a clearly scoped interim service priced as its own engagement, and never start without the evidence obligations satisfied

edge_cases.description: A winnable site sits in a geography or on a shift pattern where no crew supply exists today
edge_cases.trigger: an opportunity outside every serviceable cluster or requiring an unusual access window
edge_cases.mitigation: treat it as an explicit anchor decision with travel, inspection and backfill priced in and crew supply confirmed before the proposal is sent, or decline; never win first and search for a crew afterwards

edge_cases.description: The buyer asks directly whether the cleaners will be the broker's own employees
edge_cases.trigger: an employment question during the walkthrough or the closing meeting
edge_cases.mitigation: answer plainly and consistently with the proposal's disclosure sentence, explain the accountability path and the verified insurance classes, and record the exchange in the bid file

edge_cases.description: The walkthrough happens immediately after a deep clean or during an unusually quiet week, so the building looks far cleaner than its normal state
edge_cases.trigger: site conditions observed at an unrepresentative moment
edge_cases.mitigation: ask what was done in the past week and what the site looks like at its worst, use occupancy and traffic evidence rather than the visible state, and record the visit's timing as an assumption in the register

edge_cases.description: The prospect asks for a free trial clean or a discounted first month to prove the service
edge_cases.trigger: a buyer seeking proof before committing to a term
edge_cases.mitigation: offer a short initial term with normal pricing and an inspection at its end instead of free work, and if any introductory concession is given, write its end date and reverting price into the agreement so nothing is implied

edge_cases.description: The requested scope includes work the crew cannot safely or lawfully perform, such as high-access exterior glass, biohazard remediation, roof areas or confined spaces
edge_cases.trigger: a client expectation that reaches beyond ordinary janitorial scope
edge_cases.mitigation: exclude it explicitly in the matrix, say plainly that it needs a qualified specialist, and offer to coordinate a separately contracted specialist rather than quietly accepting the work

edge_cases.description: The client returns the signed agreement with a national procurement addendum adding auto-renewal, a multi-year price freeze and broad indemnity language
edge_cases.trigger: corporate paper substituted at signature stage
edge_cases.mitigation: stop the signature, run the clause-class check, escalate the unfamiliar terms to a qualified professional, reprice for any protection removed, and decline where the exposure cannot be bounded

workflow.action: Write the broker charter, the disclosure sentence and the will-not-bid conditions
workflow.description: Fix the revenue unit, every cost class the spread must absorb, the standing refusal conditions and the plain statement of how the service is delivered
workflow.artifact: dated broker charter with the disclosure sentence and the selling constraint list
workflow.gate: the revenue unit, the absorbed cost classes, at least three will-not-bid conditions, the disclosure sentence and the four selling constraints are written and dated

workflow.action: Build the obligation register of coverage, bonding, licensing and classification questions
workflow.description: List the obligation classes this broker must be able to evidence, confirm with its own agent what is in force, and record the worker-classification question as a standing professional-verification item
workflow.artifact: obligation register with confirmation dates and open verification items
workflow.gate: every class names what evidences it, who confirmed it and on what date, and every unresolved classification or coverage question is marked for professional verification rather than assumed

workflow.action: Profile the target facility classes and the buyers inside them
workflow.description: Write the soil, fixture, floor, access and compliance profile per class the broker can actually serve, then map the signer, the process type and the decision window for each, with the cluster overlay
workflow.artifact: facility-class profile sheet with a buyer and decision-window map
workflow.gate: each pursued class carries its drivers, its compliance-class flags, a named decision role, a process type and a serviceable-cluster note

workflow.action: Screen the opportunity and diagnose the incumbent before scheduling a visit
workflow.description: Establish signer, budget, dissatisfaction class, access window, requirement classes, crew supply and payment signals, and record a bid, conditional-bid or no-bid decision
workflow.artifact: dated screening record with the incumbent failure-class diagnosis
workflow.gate: the record names the signer, the budget signal, the staffability answer, the requirement classes and an explicit decision with its reason

workflow.action: Run the walkthrough as a capture protocol
workflow.description: Walk every cleaned space and record areas, floors, fixtures, obstruction, trash haul, access constraints and the client's expectations verbatim, quoting nothing on site
workflow.artifact: walkthrough field record with dated, attributed observations
workflow.gate: every capture item is present, expectations are recorded verbatim, and no price was quoted during the visit

workflow.action: Establish cleanable area and the floor inventory
workflow.description: Measure or mark up the plan, split area by surface, separate restrooms and kitchens for fixture-based computation, and list excluded areas with the provenance of every figure
workflow.artifact: measured area and surface inventory with provenance and exclusions
workflow.gate: no figure is unsourced, gross and cleanable area are distinguished, and the excluded areas are listed

workflow.action: Write the task-and-frequency matrix with its exclusions
workflow.description: Place every task in an area at a frequency across the nightly, detail and periodic bands, write the exclusion list, and state who supplies consumables
workflow.artifact: scope-of-work matrix with exclusion list and consumables statement
workflow.gate: every priced task has an area and a frequency, periodic work sits in its own band, and the exclusion and consumables statements are present

workflow.description: Divide measured area and fixture counts by source-tagged production rates, apply the obstruction adjustment, multiply by frequency, and compute periodic hours separately
workflow.artifact: labor worksheet with per-task hours, rates and their sources
workflow.gate: every rate carries a source and an obstruction adjustment, and periodic hours appear on their own line rather than inside the nightly total

workflow.description: Convert hours into a monthly cost using the actual engagement structure, then add consumables, equipment, travel, inspections, backfill, billing and complaint allowances
workflow.artifact: monthly delivered cost build with each line tagged quoted, measured or estimated
workflow.gate: no cost line is untagged, the crew line is quoted against the written matrix, and any burden class used is marked verified or flagged for verification

workflow.action: Build the price, stress it and fix the walk-away floor
workflow.description: Add the retained spread to delivered cost, state what the spread funds, run the sensitivity tests on area, rate, crew cost, added scope, backfill and payment speed, and set the floor before any price conversation
workflow.artifact: price build with the spread's funding list, sensitivity results and a dated walk-away floor
workflow.gate: the price traces line by line to the cost build, the spread's funding list is written, and the floor and permitted non-price concessions are recorded before the client is given a number

workflow.action: Write the proposal and its differentiation section
workflow.description: Assemble the scope annex, exclusions, priced lines including periodic and optional work, the disclosure sentence, certificate classes, transition plan, inspection and response commitments and references
workflow.artifact: client proposal with signed-ready scope annex
workflow.gate: every claim is verifiable, contractual or absent; the disclosure sentence is present; each differentiating commitment names its deliverer, cadence and the cost already carried in the build

workflow.action: Check the agreement against the clause classes, then close and hand off the bid record
workflow.description: Run the clause-class check on whichever paper governs, escalate unfamiliar or control-flavored language to a qualified professional, then assemble the complete bid record and both downstream handoffs
workflow.artifact: executed agreement plus the closed bid record with its assumptions register
workflow.gate: the price-adjustment cause, the extra-work authorization and the cancellation symmetry are checked and recorded; crew sourcing has the scope, hours and constraints and margin monitoring has the cost build and assumptions before the first service night

priority_rationale: The frame units come first because the definition of the spread, the disclosure the model requires, the selling constraints and the obligation classes to be verified bound every later choice; targeting, buyer mapping and screening precede the walkthrough because scoping is the expensive step and the wrong site is best refused before it is measured; measurement precedes the labor model, the labor model precedes the cost build and the cost build precedes price and floor because each is arithmetic standing on the one before it; and the proposal, the protective clause classes and the closed bid record come last because they are where the whole build is committed to a client and handed forward to crew sourcing and margin monitoring.

dominance_rules.rule: Verification of an obligation class dominates any promise made to win a bid
dominance_rules.rationale: insurance, bonding, licensing, classification and facility-compliance duties vary by jurisdiction, client and year, and a promise made ahead of verification can be one the broker cannot legally keep
dominance_rules.trigger: a proposal, conversation or contract clause would assert a coverage, bond, licence, credential or classification fact
dominance_rules.action: name the obligation class, mark it for verification with the carrier, authority or qualified professional, and hold the promise until the verification is recorded with a date

dominance_rules.rule: Plain disclosure of the service model dominates competitive advantage
dominance_rules.rationale: the entire broker model depends on the client knowing who cleans and who is accountable; a bid won on a misunderstanding is a liability rather than an asset
dominance_rules.trigger: a competitive framing, a buyer's assumption or a direct question would be easier to answer by implying an in-house workforce
dominance_rules.action: state the delivery model plainly in the document and in the room, and accept the lost bid if the truthful answer costs it

dominance_rules.rule: The walk-away floor dominates the desire to win the contract
dominance_rules.rationale: a contract below the cost build loses money every month for its whole term and consumes the capacity that could serve a profitable one
dominance_rules.trigger: a client's target price, or a known incumbent number, sits below the floor recorded before negotiation
dominance_rules.action: offer a scope, frequency or term alternative that fits the floor, and decline rather than sign below it

dominance_rules.rule: Measured cleanable area dominates any area figure supplied by the client or a listing
dominance_rules.rationale: gross and leased figures routinely include space the crew never enters, and an area error repeats in every month of the contract
dominance_rules.trigger: a client-supplied or listing-derived square footage is available and a measurement is not
dominance_rules.action: measure or mark up a plan before pricing; if that is impossible, price the stated assumption, label it in the proposal, and make correction a repricing event

dominance_rules.rule: Observed crew time dominates any borrowed production rate once it exists
dominance_rules.rationale: a rate observed on this broker's own crews in comparable space is direct evidence, while a published or borrowed rate is a prior from another context
dominance_rules.trigger: delivered hours from a comparable site disagree with the library rate used in a bid
dominance_rules.action: update the rate library with the observed figure and its source, and reprice open bids that relied on the superseded rate

dominance_rules.rule: Written scope dominates every verbal promise made during a walkthrough
dominance_rules.rationale: the matrix is what the crew is instructed from and what any complaint is judged against, so anything outside it exists for nobody but the client's memory
dominance_rules.trigger: a task was agreed to on site but has not been written into the matrix
dominance_rules.action: add it to the matrix and reprice, or write it into the exclusion list, before the proposal is sent

dominance_rules.rationale: a contract nobody can crew fails immediately, damages the broker's reputation in that territory and consumes the response capacity promised to paying accounts
dominance_rules.trigger: no crew supply is confirmed for the site's geography, access window or facility class
dominance_rules.action: confirm crew supply before the proposal is sent, or record an explicit anchor decision with its added cost, or decline the opportunity

dominance_rules.rule: Factual description dominates fear as a selling instrument
dominance_rules.rationale: health, liability and inspection anxieties are easy levers and destroy the trust the recurring model depends on, particularly with less sophisticated buyers
dominance_rules.trigger: a real observed condition could be escalated into a warning that pressures the buyer to decide now
dominance_rules.action: state the observation once, factually and in writing, and let the scope and price answer it without escalation

dominance_rules.rule: Client-facing commitments never exceed what the handoff has been told and funded
dominance_rules.rationale: an inspection cadence, response time or staffing continuity promised but not costed and not communicated to the crew becomes a broken promise in the first month
dominance_rules.trigger: a proposal or negotiation would add a service commitment after the cost build was completed
dominance_rules.action: cost the commitment, carry it into the price, and write it into the crew-facing handoff, or leave it out of the proposal

anti_rework_rules.rule: Screen the opportunity before scheduling the walkthrough
anti_rework_rules.prevents: spending a site visit, a full scope build and a proposal on a buyer who cannot sign, has no budget, or only needs a comparison quote

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pull the client's own insurance, bonding and licensing demands before any pricing work begins
anti_rework_rules.prevents: repricing an entire bid, or winning a contract that cannot start, after discovering required limits, endorsements or bond classes late

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm crew supply for the geography, shift and facility class before the proposal is sent
anti_rework_rules.prevents: winning a contract that must then be staffed at any cost, or handed back, both of which damage the territory

anti_rework_rules.rule: Measure cleanable area and split it by surface before applying any production rate
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rebuilding the entire labor model, cost build and price when the area or surface mix turns out to be wrong

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the task-and-frequency matrix and its exclusion list before quoting any number
anti_rework_rules.prevents: recurring unpaid work and the month-two argument about what the client believed was included

anti_rework_rules.rule: Price periodic work and consumables on their own lines before assembling the monthly figure
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering the cost of a refinishing cycle or a paper-goods obligation only when it comes due, with no mechanism to charge for it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Settle any control-of-worker language with a qualified professional before it enters a proposal or an agreement
anti_rework_rules.prevents: having to renegotiate signed commitments, or unwind an arrangement, after a classification question is raised

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the walk-away floor and the permitted non-price concessions before the first price conversation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: conceding price inside a negotiation and discovering afterwards that the contract cannot fund the service it promised

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record every assumption with the bid rather than after the win
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an unattributable margin drift later, and a dispute with both the crew and the client about what was actually priced

iteration_protocol.trigger: delivered crew hours on a won site differ materially from the hours the bid modelled
iteration_protocol.action: re-measure the site if needed, correct the rate library entry with the observed figure and its source, and reprice open bids that used the superseded rate

iteration_protocol.trigger: a scope dispute or an extra-work request appears in the first weeks of a new contract
iteration_protocol.action: trace the gap back to the matrix and the walkthrough record, add the missing task or exclusion to the bid template, and re-issue the crew-facing scope

iteration_protocol.trigger: a client, landlord or authority changes an insurance, bonding, licensing or facility-compliance requirement
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify the affected obligation classes with the carrier or authority, price any new gap, and update every open bid that relies on the old requirement set

iteration_protocol.trigger: crew quotes or supply costs drift in a territory
iteration_protocol.action: rebuild the cost line for open bids in that territory, recompute their walk-away floors, and check whether the price-adjustment cause in pending agreements covers the drift

iteration_protocol.trigger: a client demands direction over individual crew members, exclusivity, or named individuals in the agreement
iteration_protocol.action: hold the clause, route it to a qualified professional in the operating jurisdiction, and offer outcome, inspection and continuity commitments in its place until the verification is recorded

iteration_protocol.trigger: the walkthrough reveals conditions materially different from what the screening call described
iteration_protocol.action: return to the screen, re-decide bid or no-bid on the observed facts, and restate the incumbent diagnosis before any scope or price work continues

iteration_protocol.trigger: bids are being lost in a consistent pattern at a consistent stage
iteration_protocol.action: review the closed records for that stage, retune the screen, the buyer map or the differentiation set, and check whether the losses cluster near the floor rather than far above it

iteration_protocol.trigger: win rate improves while the delivered spread on new accounts falls
iteration_protocol.action: re-examine the price build and the sensitivity assumptions for recent wins, and raise the floor or restore the cost lines that were quietly trimmed to win
